source.title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions

accepted.question_text: For operator classes K_FNO^alpha consisting of maps that can be approximated efficiently by Fourier Neural Operators, current theory gives a lower and upper bound on the optimal algebraic minimax sample-complexity exponent with upper endpoint 1/2. Is 1/2 the true sharp exponent for these architecture-defined classes, or is the present gap between lower and upper bounds only an artifact of the ERM-based analysis?

evidence.quote: Thm. 5 shows that the optimal algebraic minimax rate exponent is asymptotically 1/2 as alpha -> infinity.

The gap between the upper and lower bound in (10) for finite alpha is likely due to the ERM proof technique for the lower bound. It is of interest to determine whether the exponent 1/2 is sharp or not.

accepted.question_text: Can one separate more clearly the minimax sample complexities of holomorphic operator classes H(b) o iota and architecture-defined classes K_FNO^alpha by either proving lower bounds for the FNO-based class or proving that the holomorphic classes are well approximated by Fourier Neural Operators?

evidence.quote: Taken together, the results in section 2 and section 3 imply that max{s_n (H (b) o iota)L^2_varrho, s_n (K^alpha_FNO)L^2_varrho} <= s_n (K_Lip)L^2_varrho. A further separation of the left-hand side would require lower bounds on s_n (K^alpha_FNO)L^2_varrho or showing that elements of H (b) o iota are well approximated by FNOs.

accepted.question_text: When learning holomorphic operators by empirical risk minimization with fully trainable neural networks, especially in the noise-free setting, are faster-than-Monte Carlo convergence rates achievable?
accepted.context_brief: Fast ERM rates with trainable networks

evidence.quote: Based on the results presented in section 2, it is natural to ask whether faster-than-Monte Carlo rates are possible when considering ERM with fully trainable networks, especially in the absence of noise.

accepted.question_text: In operator learning for holomorphic operators using empirical risk minimization with fully trainable multilayer perceptrons and i.i.d. statistical noise, current bounds are at best of order n^(-1/2). Is that n^(-1/2) rate merely an artifact of the statistical-learning proof in the noisy setting, or is it a genuine minimax barrier for this problem?

evidence.quote: The error bound in (4) exhibits an approximate Monte Carlo rate when r -> infinity, t -> infinity, and tau -> 0, with the right-hand side approaching n^(-1/2).
Another key difference concerns the network class N. In Thm. 1, N contains fully trainable, unconstrained MLPs.
A remaining question is whether the nonparametric rate in Thm. 1 (which is at best n^(-1/2)) is an artifact of the statistical learning analysis in the noisy setting, or a genuine minimax barrier.

accepted.question_text: For operator learning with observations corrupted by random noise of level sigma, can one derive a minimax theory whose rates depend explicitly on both the sample size n and the noise level sigma, analogous to the noise-aware characterizations known in classical function approximation?

evidence.quote: To address observations corrupted by random noise, e.g., as in Thm. 1, let eta be a centered probability measure on V and define the statistical nonlinear sampling n-width s~^eta_n (K; sigma)_X by
Here sigma > 0 is the noise level.
An open problem is to obtain a similar noise level aware characterization of minimax rates for operator learning.

accepted.question_text: Which classes of operators arising in scientific applications are practically relevant while still admitting algebraic minimax sample complexity for operator learning?

evidence.quote: Another important challenge is to identify classes of operators that are practically relevant in scientific applications, but still enjoy algebraic minimax sample complexity.

accepted.question_text: For the holomorphic operator classes used in the empirical-risk-minimization results, can one prove sharp bounds for the statistical nonlinear sampling width under noisy observations, so that one can determine whether faster-than-Monte Carlo rates are possible under suitable statistical noise models?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp noisy bounds for holomorphic classes

evidence.quote: First, can one prove sharp bounds on the statistical n-width s~^eta_n (K; sigma)L^2_varrho (11) for K the holomorphic classes considered in Thms. 1-2? This will help clarify whether faster-than-Monte Carlo rates are possible or not under suitable statistical noise models.

accepted.question_text: Is empirical risk minimization minimax-optimal for target classes beyond holomorphic operators, such as C-infinity operator classes or classes arising from specific parametric PDE problems?

evidence.quote: Moreover, is ERM optimal in the minimax sense of (8) for target classes beyond holomorphic operators? Other sets of interest could include C^infinity operators or those arising from specific parametric PDE problems.
